summary.text: Mark Davis, a U.S. Air Force veteran and small-business owner with no party affiliation, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the open 16th Congressional District seat in Florida to Sydney Gruters.
His campaign materials describe him as a political newcomer who moved to Florida about four years ago and entered the race after a public confrontation with the governor over health care.

paragraphs.text: Davis earned a high school diploma from Western High School and served in the U.S. Air Force from 2005 to 2013.
He describes himself as a father, veteran and small-business owner who has worked in healthcare, and his campaign website says he moved to Florida about four years ago.
Davis says he is not a politician and built an online following before running.
In his Candidate Connection survey he says he saw corruption up close in healthcare, spoke up, and then confronted the governor face to face, and that he supports a single-payer health system.
He lists affordable healthcare, protecting freedoms, economic security and restoring truth to government as his priorities.
During the campaign, he said he was running on health care, economic security and what he calls accountability in government.
He received 1.8% of the vote to Sydney Gruters's 51.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

WWSB reported that Davis was arrested on July 28, 2026, for obstructing an officer without violence during a court-ordered welfare check of his children by Department of Children and Families investigators.
Davis told ABC7 the complaint is false and is retaliation for his criticism of President Trump and Gov. DeSantis.
This is a misdemeanor charge, not a conviction.
